verdicts.reason: rule 2 broken promise: hook 'My sister wants lost-proof socks for Christmas' sets up a gift story, but the sister and Christmas never come back; the body is a self-purchase ('so I ordered them to prove a point', 'my drawer actually looks like an adult lives here now'), so ordering a gift 'to prove a point' doesn't make sense

rule 3 contradiction (attitude): the narrator's own VO presents the socks as a recommendation ('Gift guide pick: socks that can't get lost.') and the next line mocks it ('like who needs that'); it only works if you add 'I saw a...' in your head, and the skeptic body ('so I ordered them to prove a point') does not fit someone who just recommended them. Also rule 2: the gift framing never pays off, since nothing in the body is about giving them to anyone
